payload.claim: Every witness in this diff builds its worktree with git's default (sha1) hash algorithm, and `GIT_DEFAULT_HASH=sha256` in the criterion-3 test only changes what a naive `git init` inside the script would default to — it never changes the *existing* worktree's own format, which `rev-parse --show-object-format` still reports as sha1. So replacing the dynamic `fmt=$($worktree_prefix rev-parse --show-object-format)` with a hardcoded `fmt="sha1"` leaves every test in this diff green, including the criterion-3 witness, because in no test does the real worktree's object format ever differ from sha1. A target repo whose worktree is genuinely sha256 would get a fresh dir pinned to the wrong format (`--object-format=sha1` while the alternates objects are sha256, or vice versa on a hardcoded-sha256 mutant), and `export_patch` would fail on every attempt with no witness to catch the regression.
